Its evidence, verbatim:


Summary, verbatim: *"32×32 PNG icon-sized raster. SVG would scale cleanly across DPIs and ship smaller; the current asset locks the image to a single resolution."*

`effort: "quick"`, `fix_shape: "ship the SVG source; rasters lose at any scale"`, and the suggested action is `switch_to_svg_icon`.

## Why a new SVG indicator beats another 32×32 PNG

**32 × 32 px is the whole asset — there is no headroom.** A PNG at those dimensions stores exactly 1,024 pixels. Anything that renders it larger than 1× — a 2× or 3× display, a user with browser zoom, a settings page that shows the indicator at 40px — resamples those same 1,024 pixels and you get soft edges. The scanner's phrasing is the honest one: *"locks the image to a single resolution."* The PNG pattern's implicit cost is that "copy the pattern" really means "ship `@1x`, `@2x`, `@3x`" — three assets and a naming convention, before you've drawn anything.

**A status indicator multiplies that cost by its states.** Unlike a static check mark, an indicator has ok / warning / error / idle variants. In PNG that's states × DPIs files, each one a separate binary an agent or designer can update in isolation and leave stale. An SVG is one file whose fill can be `currentColor` or a CSS custom property — the state lives in the stylesheet next to the rest of your status colors, not in a folder of near-identical PNGs. That's the argument the scan doesn't make and the one that actually decides it here.

**At icon complexity, vector is also literally smaller.** A check mark or a filled dot is two or three path commands. Below the 64px threshold the detector uses, path data beats a pixel grid on bytes — hence *"smaller bytes"* in the evidence.

## The trap to avoid on the way

Don't take "make it an SVG" as license to export whatever the design tool emits. The highest-severity asset finding in this same repo is exactly that failure — `crime_00032`, **SVG With Embedded Raster**, severity `high`, on `src/assets/partner-logo.svg`:

```
"2 `<image href=\"data:image/…;base64,…\">` occurrences"
"embedded MIME types: image/jpeg, image/png"
"SVG byte size: 592 bytes (includes the base64 overhead)"
```

That file has the `.svg` extension and none of the benefits — the pixels are still locked to one resolution, now with base64 overhead on top. So: real vector paths, no `<image href="data:...">`.

## Scope check

`crime_00036` is `severity: low` / `agent_risk: 0.16` — it is not telling you to go fix `check-icon.png` right now. It's telling you not to propagate the pattern into a new asset, which is the cheapest moment to get it right. If you do want the existing one converted too, that's a separate `effort: "quick"` change and I'd do it as its own commit.
